A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same DP-GRAPE work. Their main text, figures, tables, algorithms, and Appendices A-D are readable and support comparison despite reformatting and relocation of material.

before.justification: v1 reports original DP-GRAPE training and fine-tuning results, memory measurements, timing experiments, and supplementary analyses in Section 5 and Appendix C.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical results and adds a projection-dimension sensitivity experiment in Appendix C.2 and Figure 5.

M1.justification: Algorithm 1 changes from adding noise to the clipped-gradient sum before dividing by B to adding noise after averaging. At fixed sigma, the written noise variance therefore changes from C²sigma²/B² to C²sigma². The projection, clipping, and Adam components remain intact; an implementation change or experimental rerun is not established.

E1.justification: The ViT, RoBERTa, and OPT datasets and tasks are retained. The new rank study reuses SST-2, SNLI, and TREC under existing task conditions. SQuAD and DROP results already appeared in v1's appendix.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged in the corresponding experiments, including naive DP-GaLore, DP-Adam, DP-LoRA, and DPZero. The new rank study evaluates DP-GRAPE alone. The cited non-private ViT accuracies added to Figure 2's caption provide context rather than a new matched experimental baseline.

E3.justification: Appendix C.2 adds a protocol sweeping r over 4, 8, 16, 32, 64, 128, and 256 at epsilon 2 and 6, with clipping thresholds selected separately for each rank and dataset. The settings of the retained benchmark experiments are unchanged.

E4.justification: v2 adds a focused utility-versus-rank ablation on three RoBERTa datasets in Figure 5. v1 already examined rank versus memory, but did not report this accuracy sensitivity study. Existing spectral, memory, and convergence analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions report three-seed means and standard errors for the retained language-model benchmark tables. The new rank study also averages three seeds, without introducing a new uncertainty estimator, significance test, or increased run count for matched experiments.

E6.justification: The retained numerical result tables and original plots are unchanged, including v1 Table 12, relocated to v2 Table 5. New Figure 5 reports substantial accuracy degradation at large r on SNLI and TREC, while SST-2 remains comparatively stable.

T1.justification: Theorems 4.1 and D.10 revise the reported leading stationarity bound by removing its sqrt(L) factor. Appendix D adds the assumption r <= d - 1, corrects Gaussian-moment formulas in Lemmas D.5 and D.8, and substantially revises clipping and noise calculations. It also adds privacy arguments concerning known projectors, post-processing, and adjacency conventions.

C1.justification: The introduction replaces the contribution claiming random projections match SVD performance with the more specific finding that privatization flattens gradient spectra. The abstract adopts this motivation. The headline memory-saving, comparable-utility, pretraining, and 6.7B scalability claims remain.

C2.justification: v2 adds a hypothesis linking large-r degradation to projection variance and injected noise. Section 5.3 explains why memory savings relative to non-private Adam depend on model and batch size. The conclusion also develops the proposed combination with randomized gradient-norm estimation.

D1.justification: v2 supplies a project-code URL absent from v1 and documents the new rank study's clipping search and averaging procedure. Existing hardware, training budgets, and main experiment hyperparameters are retained. The linked repository's availability was not independently checked.

R1.justification: v2 expands the focused comparison with LoRA, DP-LoRA, and GaLore. It adds references for alternative privacy notions and non-private ViT context, and replaces the earlier optimality discussion with a DP-SGD rate comparison citing Wang et al. (2017). The overall research positioning remains similar.

P1.justification: Targeted rewrites clarify the abstract, contributions, methodology, and conclusion. Background subsections become unnumbered headings, the projected Adam routine receives an explicit name, and a Broader Impact Statement is added. The main narrative and appendix organization remain recognizable.

P2.justification: Document-wide journal reformatting changes typography, text width, author presentation, running headers, and table styling. Figure 1 is relocated, the OPT generation table moves from the appendix into the main text, and a new three-panel rank-sensitivity figure is added. Existing charts are resized and repositioned.

improvement.justification: v2 adds useful evidence for choosing projection rank, documents code access, and explains the conditions governing memory advantages. Appendix D fixes explicit Gaussian-moment errors and clarifies privacy reasoning. These improve support and clarity, although residual inconsistencies between Theorem D.10 and the final displayed bound limit confidence in the revised theoretical guarantee.
